doc.title: Frank Alkyer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 10, 2020

title: DownBeat's target audience and free student subscriptions
summary: Alkyer describes readers by psychographics, with musicians first and then fans, and the free copies and digital subscriptions given to students.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Do you think, well you probably know this — what’s your target audience?

Yeah. People always ask me for demographics, and I go I can’t give you demographics. I can but DownBeat is a psychographic. We use psychographics. People who are educated or will be educated, love music, generally play music or have played music or will play music, want the better things in life, love the arts, and they could be 13, they could be 89. And that’s who it is. Because that 13-year-old is going to grow up to be that person over there and they may be a musician or they may be a lawyer or a doctor or — we’re a magazine for readers. And we become for readers at a very young age. So I always look at it like our target audience is, it’s like where do you go in this world to get your audience? And we always look at it as we really focus on musicians first and then fans of jazz want to feel like they’re backstage with the musicians. So they come next. So basically the people that come to festivals and things like that. And then anybody else that wants to come along for the ride is good. But you know it’s like, for example, we give out 15,000 copies a month during the school year to junior high, high school and college students. Free. We just tell — steal this magazine. We give it to their band director, we give it to their professors, if you’re in college you can go to DownBeat.com

and sign up for a free digital subscription for as long as you’re in school, all you have to do is tell us what year you are in school, where you are at, what your instrument is, what you’re doubling on, and you know, that’s it. Four quick questions and you get a free digital subscription for as long as you’re in school. Because that’s our next generation.
You’re setting up for the future.
Yeah. It’s like, you know, I learned from going to church on Sundays that to get people into the Kingdom of Jazz you reach them when they’re children.
